title: Add ONE opposite-signed diagnostic cell per model (direction ordering)
motivation: The primary test is fixed-workpoint transfer and stays exactly as frozen. It compares alpha=0 against the workpoint read from the GSM8K record, and that comparison alone cannot show whether the DIRECTION continues on the other side of zero. One opposite-signed cell per model makes the ordering readable.
binding_constraints: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. The reverse cell is NOT part of the primary test and is NOT in the Holm family (m=2 stays the two workpoint contrasts).

It MUST NOT redefine the BBH workpoint. alpha stays read from the frozen GSM8K record (llama -6 / qwen +8); this protocol never searches doses, and a reverse cell that happened to score higher would NOT become the workpoint.
Refused until BOTH the alpha=0 and the workpoint cell exist, so it can never be mistaken for the dose search that produced the workpoint.
All THREE cells of one model stay on that model's original physical GPU (llama GPU 0, qwen GPU 1): they are paired per-item contrasts and bf16 greedy is not byte-reproducible across GPUs.
A reverse cell is a single point, so it can show that an ordering CONTINUES or BREAKS; it cannot establish a dose-response curve or an optimum.
what_it_cannot_show: Three points do not make a curve. An ordering consistent with -6 > 0 > +4 is consistent with a monotone direction over the sampled range; it does not locate a peak, does not establish an inverted-U, and does not license calling +4 an overshoot point.
code_changes: run_bbh_numeric.sh: new REVERSE step, per-model AREV/REVTAG, refusal until alpha=0 and workpoint both exist. STAGE0 and WORKPOINT byte-unchanged in behaviour (verified by driving the launcher with real arguments).
eval_bbh_numeric.py: REVERSE = {llama3: 4, qwen2.5: -6} added to the alpha allowlist and reported in a SEPARATE diagnostic block, never folded into the Holm family or the transfer table.
